page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is network-based with a local capacity of 1 GB, and no dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and memory performance show notable limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also weak at 223.21 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 29.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth achieves an average tier rating of 28.99 GB/sec.

Given the high single-core compute capabilities paired with lower multi-core and database performance (PassMark database operations scored in the bottom 10%), this server is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic static web serving, or small-scale development environments. It is less optimal for heavy database operations or multi-threaded parallel processing. The resource density offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or local NVMe storage.
